messages:
laura (Acme): Hey team — we have an urgent customer question. They think some chat records were deleted but need an export for an audit. Ticket SUP-8291. Can you confirm default retention and exact timelines for deletion? Also need to know if audit logs and encryption keys (KMS/HSM) are exportable.

maria (Support): Hi @laura, sorry to hear that. Can you confirm whether the org is on hosted or private deployment, and whether they've set any custom retention? Also which workspace/organization ID?

laura (Acme): Hosted. Org ID is org_6X9. They say they didn't modify retention in the console. They need a full export of audit logs + any messages still available before deletion.

maria (Support): OK thanks. Default retention for hosted is 90 days for user payloads unless a custom policy is applied; audit logs are retained for 365 days by default. I'll start an export job for the audit logs and check the message retention records. Filing an internal escalation to security to confirm KMS/HSM constraints. @dylan can you chime in on key exportability?

sam (Engineering): Quick note — backend deletion is eventually consistent. Deletions trigger a background job; metadata may remain visible for a short window but payloads are removed per policy. If the customer saw deletion earlier, it could be the scheduled deletion job completed. I can check job run history for org_6X9.

maria (Support): Raised SUP-8291-ESCL, I've kicked off an audit log export to S3 (placeholder link) and requested a partial payload snapshot. ETA for export prep ~2 hours. Will update here once the file is ready.

dylan (Security): Hi all — for hosted customers we manage KMS keys; material in HSM is never exportable as raw key material. We can provide encrypted artifacts and a key-wrap proof if needed for compliance. If the customer is requesting key export, that's not possible for hosted. For Private deployments where you manage the HSM/KMS, keys belong to the customer.

laura (Acme): They asked if there is a legal-hold option to prevent scheduled deletion while audit is ongoing. Is that possible?

maria (Support): We have a temporary retention hold we can apply per-org to pause deletion jobs. It requires a support ticket and security approval. @dylan can approve the hold once we confirm scope. If approved, deletion is paused immediately and a note is added to the retention audit trail.

dylan (Security): Approved conditional on documented reason. Applying retention hold for org_6X9 now. Note: hold suspends new deletions but cannot restore already-purged payloads. I'll add a short rationale in the security log.

maria (Support): Holding applied. Export job in progress; sharing S3 link once ready. Action items: 1) sam to check deletion job history and confirm which items were purged and when, 2) dylan applied retention hold, 3) provide audit log export to customer, 4) advise on KMS — hosted keys cannot be exported.

sam (Engineering): Checked job history — deletion sweep for org_6X9 ran at 2025-05-10T14:02Z and removed items older than 90 days per default policy. I attached truncated job log snippet:```
[2025-05-10T14:02:03Z] sweep(org_6X9): matched=1240, deleted=1187, errors=0
```

maria (Support): Thanks @sam. @laura — summary for customer: default message retention is 90 days (hosted) and audit logs 365 days. We applied a temporary legal/retention hold so no further deletions will occur while you retrieve exports. We cannot export KMS private key material for hosted customers; we can provide encrypted archives and HSM wrap proofs. Export link will be sent to the ticket. Anything else urgent? :white_check_mark:

laura (Acme): That's perfect, thanks. I'll relay to their compliance team and follow up in SUP-8291 for the download link and documentation they need for the audit. Appreciated.

ops-oncall: FYI — scheduled deletion sweeps run daily at 14:02 UTC. If you need a change to the cadence or a policy exception for more than 30 days, ops + security sign-off required.
